items.title: Arvind Kejriwal Gets Death Threat, Allegedly From Lawrence Bishnoi Gang
points: The police are investigating a death threat against former Delhi chief minister and Aam Aadmi Party chief Arvind Kejriwal, allegedly issued in the name of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, with the caller demanding Rs 7 crore.

The threat was reported by Tilak Nagar MLA Jarnail Singh, who told the Delhi Police that he had received a phone call and a WhatsApp message from a person claiming to be a member of the gang with links abroad.

In a complaint filed with the police in Punjab's Mohali on November 6, Singh said the caller demanded Rs 7 crore and threatened to kill Kejriwal and his daughter, Harshita Kejriwal, if the money was not paid.
The police in Mohali have filed a case under both the BNS and the IT Act, and have given the case to an officer of the cyber crime unit identified as Sunil Kumar.
Investigators said they are examining call records, internet protocol logs and location data linked to the mobile number used to issue the threat.

points: On November 11, five stocks in the Nifty500 with a change of more than 5% appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data.
A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest.
The pattern is represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and little or no lower shadow.
It reflects strong upward price movement during the session, with the price moving from the opening level toward the session high by the close.
The pattern is commonly studied in technical analysis as an indicator of price momentum.

items.title: Why rising ammonia in Yamuna threatens Delhi’s drinking water supply
points: Ammonia levels in the Yamuna at Wazirabad have climbed to 1.5-2 parts per million (ppm), above the 0.9 ppm threshold beyond which Delhi's water supply operations begin to be affected.
Delhi Jal Board (DJB) officials say the treatment plants can handle ammoniacal nitrogen concentrations of around 1 ppm through conventional chlorination.
The latter involves two parallel drains, DD-6, carrying industrial waste, and DD-8, carrying freshwater, which run alongside each other for nearly 10km.
Delhi typically witnesses 15-22 such episodes annually, with ammonia levels crossing 1 ppm and sometimes remaining elevated for several days.
After Wazirabad, the Najafgarh drain, which accounts for nearly 69% of the pollution load entering the Yamuna in Delhi, meets the river.
Consequently, the 22km stretch of the Yamuna in Delhi contributes roughly 75% of the river's total pollution.
A government official explained that water treatment at older plants relies on chlorination, and the supply is disrupted if ammonia levels exceed 1 ppm, which can form toxic chloramine compounds.

Buying a Used Car After Diwali? Check Pending E-Challans and Move the Insurance Before You Pay
points: Before you pay for a used car, check its registration number for pending e-challans and get the seller to clear them.
Then apply to the insurer to move the policy into your name within 14 days of the transfer, or buy a fresh policy.
Pending challans matter because an e-challan is linked to the car’s registration number, so an unpaid fine stays on the record after the car is sold.
Telangana Today reported in October 2026 that this record now surfaces before a sale, in the same way as the rest of a car’s papers.
Checking pending challans takes a few minutes on the Parivahan eChallan portal of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
Delhi Traffic Police and MahaTraffic in Maharashtra run their own, and Telangana has its own challan system.
The 14-day insurance transfer rule comes from Section 157 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Apply early, with copies of Forms 29 and 30 if the new RC has not arrived yet.

items.title: Falklands oil dispute heads for international tribunal ruling
points: The international legal battle over the Sea Lion offshore oil development near the Falkland Islands has moved a step closer to a decision, with the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) concluding two days of hearings between Argentina and…

The Hamburg-based tribunal will now deliberate on Argentina’s request for emergency measures to halt offshore drilling and the installation of production infrastructure linked to the Navitas Petroleum-operated project.
A ruling is tentatively scheduled for November 28.

During hearings on November 10 and 11, Argentina argued that allowing the project to proceed while the sovereignty dispute remains unresolved would undermine its claimed rights over the surrounding waters and risk environmental damage.

The UK rejected the arguments, maintaining that the tribunal lacks jurisdiction over what it considers an underlying sovereignty dispute and that the Falkland Islanders have the right to develop their natural resources.

items.title: DOF adds up to $160m in offshore vessel work
points: Norwegian offshore vessel owner DOF has secured a seven-year contract for an unnamed construction support vessel and an extension for the Skandi Constructor, adding between $135m and $160m in potential firm contract value.
The Oslo-listed company said the new long-term agreement covers one of its smaller construction support vessels (CSVs), including remotely operated vehicle services.
The award will add approximately $110m to DOF’s contract backlog.
Separately, DOF confirmed that an extension option has been exercised for the Skandi Constructor, keeping the vessel under firm contract until April 2028.
DOF classified the extension as substantial, representing a contract value of between $25m and $50m.
The 2009-built vessel is designed for well intervention, subsea construction, equipment installation and inspection, repair, and maintenance operations.
It has been operating offshore Guyana, where it has supported ExxonMobil’s offshore activities.

In October 2025, DOF secured one-year extensions for the Skandi Constructor and Skandi Nomad, keeping the former employed until the second quarter of 2027 and the latter until the fourth quarter of 2026.

items.title: EU clears $2.2bn support to revive Belgian offshore wind tender
points: The European Commission has approved a €2.04bn ($2.26bn) state aid scheme for Belgium’s first offshore wind farm in the Princess Elisabeth Zone, clearing the way for a new tender after the original process was cancelled last year.
The support package will cover the construction and operation of a wind farm with a planned capacity of up to 735MW, capable of generating approximately 2.6TWh of electricity annually.
The scheme will run for 20 years, with the competitive tender result expected in the fourth quarter of 2027.
The Princess Elisabeth Zone is planned to accommodate three offshore wind farms with a combined capacity of around 3.5GW.

Belgium’s federal energy minister Mathieu Bihet said the Commission’s approval removes the final obstacle to relaunching the tender, which was suspended in July 2025 amid legal, financial and technical uncertainties.

The revised framework introduces a two-way contract for difference, under which the developer receives compensation when electricity prices fall below an agreed level and pays the Belgian authorities when prices exceed it.

items.title: South Pars platform fire forces evacuation of offshore workers
points: A fire at Iran’s giant South Pars gas field forced 17 offshore workers to abandon a production platform, triggering a rescue operation in rough seas before the blaze was brought under control.
The incident occurred at approximately 7.30 pm local time on November 10 on the SPD14D platform, part of Phase 14 of the South Pars development in the Persian Gulf.
Pars Oil and Gas Company said the workers shut down production, depressurised the installation and evacuated using lifeboats.
However, strong winds and waves reaching around four metres complicated the rescue operation, and workers spent approximately 15 hours at sea.
The lifeboat was eventually secured to a rescue vessel, and all 17 workers were subsequently brought ashore safely at Nakhilu port.
The platform normally produces around 14m cu m of gas per day.
Although production from the platform was suspended, Pars Oil and Gas said the shortfall was fully offset by increased output from other South Pars installations.
